title: A duty cut wiped out his factory. He rebuilt into a Rs 12,000 crore company. October 27, 2026.
excerpt: From a freedom fighter who died demanding dignity for prisoners, to a mathematician recognized by the world's top prize for young researchers, to an institute built in a mentor's memory, to Delhi's busiest half-year ever at its airport, to an entrepreneur who lost everything and rebuilt from Sri Lanka outward - October 27's five stories are about what survives when the first attempt collapses.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about what gets built on the other side of a collapse - a hunger strike that outlasted the body attempting it, a mathematician's return after circling the globe's top departments, an institute built from grief, an airport breaking records despite a rough year for the sector, and a factory's failure that became a multinational company.

October 27, 1904: a revolutionary was born who would die 63 days into a hunger strike, demanding dignity for political prisoners

Jatindra Nath Das, arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case alongside Bhagat Singh, died in 1929 after a 63-day hunger strike demanding equal treatment for Indian political prisoners - a sacrifice that shaped how detainees were treated for years after.

He worked at Princeton, UCL and King's College London before coming home. In 2026, the world's math community gave him its top young-mathematician honour

Professor Mahesh Kakde won the 2026 ICTP/IMU Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians, becoming the fifth Indian ever to win it, after a career spanning Princeton, UCL and King's College London before returning to IISc Bengaluru in 2019.

Her husband mentored Google's founders. She just gave India its first institute for American Studies, in his memory

Asha Jadeja Motwani, widow of Stanford professor Rajeev Motwani - who mentored Larry Page and Sergey Brin - endowed $5 million to O.P. Jindal Global University in 2025, creating India's first dedicated institute for American Studies.

Delhi's airport just had its busiest first half of a fiscal year ever

Indira Gandhi International Airport handled 38.5 million passengers between April and September 2026, its highest-ever first-half total, despite known headwinds across Indian aviation this year.

A duty cut wiped out his factory. His bank reportedly took his house. He rebuilt into a company worth over Rs 12,000 crore

Rajat Agrawal's lead-recycling business collapsed in the early 1990s after an import-duty change. He rebuilt it from Sri Lanka outward into Gravita India, now valued above Rs 12,000 crore.

Five stories, one pattern: a strike that outlasted the body, a mathematician's long way home, an institute built from loss, an airport's record year despite headwinds, and a factory's collapse that became a company spanning continents.
